verses.1: And in the sixth year, Jehoida became stronger. He took the leaders of the people to help him: Elohim, son of Jerocham; and Ismael, son of Jehochanan. They were also his helpers: Elohim, son of Obed, and Elyashafat, son of Zikri. They all served him together in the covenant.
verses.2: And they went into Judah. They gathered together the people from all the cities of Judah. The leaders of the tribes also came to Jerusalem.
verses.3: And all the people made a covenant with the king in the house of God. The king said to them, “Now, the son of the king will rule, just as Jehovah has commanded concerning the descendants of David.”
verses.4: This is what the three of you shall do on Shabbat, for the priests and the Levites, at the doors of the tabernacles.
verses.5: And the third place was in the king’s house, and the third place was at the gate of the palace. And all the people were in the courtyards of the house of Jehovah.
verses.6: And the House of God shall not be entered into, except by those who serve and work for the priests. They will enter, because they are holy. And all the people shall keep the laws given by Jehovah.
verses.7: And the soldiers surrounded the king, with each one holding a weapon in his hand. They brought him into the house, and they kept watch over the king as he entered and left.
verses.8: And the Levites and all of Israel did as Jehovah commanded. The priest took one man from each family, along with those who were going out on Shabbat. For the priest was responsible for overseeing these matters.
verses.9: And the priest gave to the musicians the instruments, the trumpets, and the rulers that belonged to King David, which were kept in the house of God.
verses.10: And he made all the people stand up, and every man who was sent with a spear from the temple of the Yemanite to the temple of the Semitite, to serve and worship the king.
verses.11: And they brought out the king’s son, and they gave him the crown and the authority. Then they made him king. But Jehovah and his sons destroyed him. They said, “Long live the king!”
verses.12: And Etalya heard the voices of the people who were praising and glorifying the king. Then he went before the people to the house of Jehovah.
verses.13: And behold, the king was standing on his throne in the hall. The servants and women stood around him. All the people of the land were rejoicing and singing in the halls. The musicians played their instruments, and they praised God. At that moment, Atalia tore her clothes and said, “Tie me up!”
verses.14: And the priest brought the women who were with him, along with the orders given by the king. He said to them, “Go into the house of the queen. She will die in Harb, because the priest said that she should not be killed in the house of Jehovah.”
verses.15: They put their hands on her, and she entered the courtyard of the chariots. There, they killed her.
verses.16: And Jehovah will make a covenant between him and all the people, and between him and the king, so that they may become a people of Jehovah.
verses.17: And all the people came into the house of the priest. They destroyed his offerings and his idols. They also killed the priest, who was a priestly officer, before the altar.
verses.18: And Jehovah’s servant put up the pillars of the Temple of Jehovah in the hands of the priests. These priests were descendants of David. They carried out the work of building the Temple of Jehovah, as written in Moses’ laws. This was done with joy and song, by the hands of David.
verses.19: And the scribes stood outside the doors of the Temple of Jehovah, and the unclean person could not enter for any reason.
verses.20: And he took the rulers and the mighty men, and all those who ruled over the people. He brought the king down from the house of God. They entered through the upper gate of the king’s palace. Then they placed the king on the throne.
verses.21: And all the people of the land rejoiced. The city was peaceful. And Etalya was killed in battle.
